ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Impatience.cs:17-20) == cost 0 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF.

OnPlay.rationale: `if (!PileType.Hand.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Any(c => c.Type == CardType.Attack)) await CardPileCmd.Draw(..., Cards.BaseValue, Owner)` (Impatience.cs:29-32) == `if not any(c.card_type == CardType.ATTACK for c in ctx.player.hand): DrawCmd.draw(ctx.player, self._cards)`. The condition is checked at play time and Impatience itself is out of the hand on both sides (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim) -- and it is a Skill anyway, so it could not satisfy the Attack test. Presentation, folded in: ShouldGlowGoldInternal (13), which is the same predicate driving the gold-glow highlight.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Cards.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Impatience.cs:24) == `self._cards += 1` (2 -> 3). Note C# declares OnUpgrade before OnPlay in this file; no behavioural consequence.
